title: Grand Romania Self-Drive: Transylvania, Maramureș, Bukovina's Painted Monasteries and the Danube Delta in 16 Days
meta_title: Romania Self-Drive 16 Days: Transylvania to Danube Delta
meta_description: 16-day Romania self-drive: Sibiu, Sighișoara, Maramureș villages, Bukovina's painted monasteries, Brașov, Bran Castle and the Danube Delta.
tagline: Saxon citadels, wooden churches, painted monasteries and the wild Danube Delta
facts: Bucharest 1, Sibiu 2, Sighișoara 2, Maramureș 2, Bukovina 2, Miercurea Ciuc 1, Brașov 2, Danube Delta 2, Bucharest 1
Rental car with GPS, plus boats in the Delta
May to June, September to October
intro: A complete self-drive loop of Romania with family-run guesthouses and guided city tours. Cross the Carpathians to Sibiu, sleep inside the citadel of Sighișoara, visit the Saxon fortified churches, then the wooden villages of Maramureș with its steam forest railway and Merry Cemetery, the painted monasteries of Bukovina, the Bicaz Gorge, Brașov with Bran and Peleș castles, and finally the Danube Delta. Two days are long: Brașov to Tulcea is about 350 km (5 to 6 hours) before the boat, and the public boat leaves at a fixed time, so we start very early or book a private boat transfer. A local travel assistant is on call by phone throughout, as well as our own 24/7 desk.

good_to_know.title: Driving in Romania
good_to_know.text: Indian licence holders need an International Driving Permit. Buy the road vignette (rovinieta) online before you drive. Village roads have horse carts, cattle and slow tractors; drive in daylight.

good_to_know.title: Bears
good_to_know.text: Romania has Europe's largest brown bear population. Never feed or approach bears by the roadside, and keep car windows closed if one is near.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in lei (RON), never in INR. Cards work in towns; carry lei in cash for village guesthouses, fuel stations and monastery entries.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

faqs.q: Can we do it with a driver instead?
faqs.a: Yes. A private driver-guide removes the long driving days and parking worries. We can quote both.

faqs.q: Do we need a separate visa for Romania?
faqs.a: Romania is a full Schengen member, so a Schengen visa covers it.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

dining_intro: Vegetarian food is easy to find in every city on this route; Jain meals take planning. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and tour, and list Indian and vegetarian restaurants near each hotel in your travel pack.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
